newsitem.title: USA: Massachusetts to oversee GE insurer liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Massachusetts to oversee GE insurer liquidation.

text.p: Massachusetts regulators have reached an agreement with General Electric (GE) to oversee the liquidation of its insolvent liability insurer despite its location in Bermuda.

The insurance division of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts said it filed a petition with the Supreme Court of Suffolk County to initiate a U.S. liquidation proceeding for the insurer, Electric Mutual Liability Insurance Co (EMLICO).

The division said the commissioner of insurance, Linda Ruthardt, had also filed a petition with the court requesting its approval of a receivers' agreement with the Bermuda Joint Liquidators of the insurer.
A division official said the commissioner will not fine GE as part of the agreement.
A spokesman for GE, which was the insurer's sole creditor and policy holder, said the company was "satisfied" with the agreement.
EMLICO, whose sole creditor and policy holder is GE, relocated to Bermuda from Beverly, Mass in June 1995 only to declare insolvency four months later amid massive environmental claims.
Its reinsurers like General Re Corp later said state regulators had been misled into approving the redomestication so that the company could take advantage of the Caribbean island's liquidation laws.
Under the laws, GE would have more say in the proceedings and the reinsurers would owe the company much greater sums than under U.S. laws.
GE said the reinsurers were trying to avoid paying the bills.
The company spokesman could not quantify the value of the claims faced by the insurer.
